<!-- DRAFT — general-lesson spin-off from the trade-promotion project. -->

The one-line version: a global demand model is easy to train and quietly wrong on the weeks that matter — promotions. Per-series models fix the accuracy, and hand you an orchestration-and-cost problem instead.

## Why global models under-forecast promos

\<The pooling effect: promo response varies too much across SKUs to share.\>

## The part nobody warns you about

\<Training 300k+ models means the bottleneck moves from modeling to distributed execution, retraining cadence, and cost.\>

## Takeaway

Pick the granularity your *decision* needs, then budget for the infrastructure it implies.
